case.initial_facts:
A man in his early forties with multiple sclerosis has received ocrelizumab for 10.6 years, with 23 infusions. New respiratory illness develops five weeks after his last infusion. His pre-symptom IgG is 422 mg/dL.
HRCT shows ground-glass change with peripheral/migratory consolidation. BAL has 69.7% lymphocytes, 25% macrophages, 4% neutrophils and 1.3% eosinophils. SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. Smoking history is negative. Cryobiopsy findings, other microbiological results, treatment response and subsequent drug decisions are not available in this packet. Exact respiratory symptoms are not allocated to this patient in the source table.

case.hidden: Patient 1 later had cryobiopsy support, clinical recovery and resumed ocrelizumab. The series-wide mean restart delay is not this patient’s documented delay. Other patients’ fatal outcomes are not this patient’s outcome.
case.reference: Use the patient-specific timing, immune context, imaging and BAL without adding all symptoms listed for the group. Negative SARS-CoV-2 does not exclude every infection. The pattern can support an organising/inflammatory lung process, while a drug-specific causal conclusion remains provisional. Proportionate pulmonary/neurology assessment, remaining microbiology and relevant tissue evidence can be discussed. Do not claim that IgG decline proves the mechanism or prescribe a steroid regimen from this packet.
